image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a European fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra). The image focuses on the head and upper torso. The subject displays the characteristic glossy black skin with large, irregular bright yellow patches covering the top of the head and back. The skin appears wet and glandular. One eye is clearly visible, appearing dark and protruding. A portion of a forelimb is visible in the lower left, showing black skin with small yellow spots. The background is out-of-focus earthy tones.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and flattened with prominent parotoid glands (poison glands) behind the eyes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head shape is consistent with the species, appearing broad. The area behind the eye shows the characteristic swelling associated with parotoid glands, though the extreme close-up makes distinct gland boundaries slightly soft.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are small, dark, and protruding with gold-flecked irises.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye is dark and protruding, but the resolution and lighting prevent the verification of 'gold-flecked irises'. The iris appears uniformly dark/black in this specific crop.
The visible portion of the torso appears thick and robust, consistent with the cylindrical body description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Vivid black and yellow (or orange) warning coloration: glossy black dorsal surface with irregular yellow spots, stripes, or bands.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is vivid and matches the species pattern perfectly. The contrast between the glossy black and bright yellow is sharp and natural.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is smooth, moist, and glandular with a glossy, wet-looking appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Specular highlights on the black skin areas strongly indicate a moist, glossy texture typical of amphibian skin.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with four digits on forelimbs and five on hindlimbs; digits are blunt and unwebbed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only a small portion of a forelimb is visible in the bottom left corner. It is too blurry and cropped to count digits or verify if they are unwebbed.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and shorter than body length, with a rounded tip.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is completely outside the frame of this close-up image.

artifact_observations.location: Yellow patch on top of head
artifact_observations.reasoning: The yellow skin texture has a slightly 'pebbled' or noisy appearance compared to the smoother black skin. While real salamander skin can be textured, this specific noise pattern resembles slight AI generation artifacting or over-sharpening rather than natural biological pores.

The forelimb exhibits significant motion blur or depth-of-field blur that feels inconsistent with the sharpness of the eye just above it. It lacks clear structural definition, making it look somewhat 'melted' into the background.
